text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn cancelled all further negotiations with farmers groups yesterday after a farmers delegation decided not to attend a scheduled meeting in his office yesterday afternoon. Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said the principle of proportionate public burdens cannot be sacrificed at the altar of concessions to farmers.

- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said yesterday that Hungary's three biggest economic dangers this year are a deterioration in the trade balance, a high deficit in the social security system and a possible 'softening' of the government's economic policy due to the elections in 1998.

- Christian Democrat president Gyorgy Giczy will deliver a speech at a rally staged by the far-right Hungarian Justice and Life Party (MIEP) on Heroes' Square on March 15. MIEP president Istvan Csurka said that farmers in Kiskoros have also decided to take part in the rally.
- President Arpad Goncz wound up an official visit to Lithuania yesterday and starts a visit to Latvia today.

- Economists and analysts of the energy sector yesterday heaped criticism on the privatisation of the Hungarian energy sector at a meeting organised by the Privatisation Research Institute and the Hungarian Energy Society.
- Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is to visit Hungary next Wednesday and Thursday.
- In the Hague on Wednesday Hungary's advocates opened up a barrage of legal arguments against the hydropower project planned by Slovakia after it unilaterally diverted the Danube in 1992.

- A senior official at the Ministry of Culture and Education said yesterday that the work of a bilateral committee on returning Hungarian artworks taken to the Soviet Union will continue in spite of yesterday's adverse decision by the Upper House of the Russian Parliament.

- The National Bank's preliminary figures considerably undervalued Hungarians's January savings, as the final data shows the increase in total net savings came to HUF 42.5 billion, as opposed to the HUF 33.3 billion reported earlier.
- The National Bank of Hungary issued samurai bonds to a value of 50 billion yesterday, its 28th bond issue in Japan.
NEPSZABADSAG

- A senior Foreign Ministry official Wednesday rejected a proposal by Jacques Klein, UN commissioner of the Serb-occupied region of eastern Croatia, that Hungary should demilitarise its border with the region.
- The Labour Supervision in Tolna county imposed the maximum fines, HUF 3 million each, on Szekszard Husipari Rt. and Metraco Rt. for multiple violations of labour rights.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The registered number of unempoloyed people grew by 23,400 last month to 498,100.
- Bid will be invited next week for 51 percent stakes in both the agricultural company Gemenc Gabona Rt. and the meat processor Ringa Rt.
- Domus, Dunaholding and Styl shares will leave the basket of the BUX Index on April 1 to be replaced by Horizon-Multiplan, the Stock Exchange Council decided.
- A new financial services company named Bond Trade Rt., established by Sputz AG, Germany's largest interbank trader of state securities, will open its doors within two weeks.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The packaging concern Dunapack Rt. will build a new plant in Romania.
